questions.question: In the following question, by using which mathematical operators will the expression become correct? 15 _ 3 _ 4 _ 20
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, by using which mathematical operators will the expression become correct?

15 _ 3 _ 4 _ 20
questions.solution:
1) ×, ÷ and > → 15 × 3 ÷ 4 > 20 → 45 ÷ 4 = 10.25 < 20 (false)

2) ÷, × and < → 15 ÷ 3 × 4 < 20 → 3 × 4 = 20 < 20 (false)

3) ÷, × and = → 15 ÷ 3 × 4 = 20 → 5 × 4 = 20 = 20 (true)

4) +, × and = → 15 + 3 × 4 = 20 → 15 + 12 = 27 ≠ 20 (false)

Hence, correct set of expression is ‘÷, × and =’.

questions.question: Ratio of present ages of P and Q is 9 : 4. The difference between their ages is 20 years. What will be the sum (in years) of their ages after 10 years?
questions.questionHtml: Ratio of present ages of P and Q is 9 : 4. The difference between their ages is 20 years. What will be the sum (in years) of their ages after 10 years?
questions.solution:
Ration of present ages of P and Q = 9 : 4 (given)

Let the age of P = 9x, age of Q = 4x

Difference between their ages = 20 years (given)

9x – 4x = 20

x = 20/5

x = 4

Present age of P = 9 × 4 = 36 years

Present age of Q = 4 × 4 = 16 years

Sum of their age after 10 years = 36 + 16 + (10 + 10) = 72 years.

Hence, answer is 72 years.

questions.question: What is full form of BOD?
questions.questionHtml: What is full form of BOD?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Biological Oxygen Demand.

  • Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), is the amount of dissolved oxygen used by microorganisms in the biological process of metabolizing organic matter in water. 
  • Water pollution by organic wastes is measured in terms of Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD).
  • BOD is the amount of dissolved oxygen needed by bacteria in decomposing the organic wastes present in water.
  • The higher value of BOD indicates low dissolved oxygen content of water and high water pollution.

Key Points

  • It is used in sewage treatment.
  • Methods used in measuring BOD.
    • Dilution method
    • Manometric method
    • Biosensor
    • Fluorescent
    • Polarographic method
    • Software sensor
    • Real-time BOD monitoring

questions.solution:
Distance covered by A in 3 seconds = 30 × 3 = 90 m

Relative velocity of B w.r.t. A = (50 – 30) m/s = 20 m/s

Now, taking A to be at rest, B has to cover 90 m to catch A

⇒ Time taken by B to catch A = 90/20 = 4.5 seconds

⇒ Total distance covered by B = 4.5 × 50 = 225 m = total distance covered by A

Let the work done by A in 1 day be p

Let work done by B in 1 day be q

questions.question: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a sum for 2 year at 20% per annum is Rs. 200. If the interest is compounded half yearly, then what is the difference (in Rs) between compound and simple interest for 1st year?
questions.questionHtml: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a sum for 2 year at 20% per annum is Rs. 200. If the interest is compounded half yearly, then what is the difference (in Rs) between compound and simple interest for 1st year?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

CI - SI for 2 years = P(R/100)2

⇒ 200 = P(20/100)2 = P(1/5)2 = P(1/25)

⇒ P = 200 × 25 = 5000 Rs.

Now,

Effective rate for SI in 1 year = 20%

Since, Interest is compounded half-yearly,

So, r = 20/2 = 10%, t = 2 cycle in 1 year

Thus,

Effective rate for CI in 2 year = 10 + 10 + (10*10)/100 = 21%

Hence, difference of interest = 21 - 20 = 1%

i.e. Difference = 1% of 5000 = 50 Rs.

∴ The correct answer is option (1).

Alternate Method

Calculation:

⇒ CI – SI = Rs. 200

Let the principal be P

So, we have

⇒ P(1 + R/100n)nt – P - (P × R × T)/100 = 200

⇒ P(1 + 20/100)2 – P - (P × 20 × 2)/100 = 200

⇒ 1.44P – P – 0.4P = 200

⇒ 0.04P = 200

⇒ P = 200/0.04 = Rs. 5000

Now, the difference when compounded half yearly

⇒ [5000(1 + 20/200)2 – 5000] – (5000 × 20 × 1)/100

⇒ [5000(1.1)2 – 5000] – 1000

⇒ [5000(1.21) – 5000] – 1000

⇒ 6050 – 6000 = Rs. 50

∴ The correct answer is option (1).

questions.question: In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. The teacher said to the student, "Have you brought your lunch?"

In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

The teacher said to the student, "Have you brought your lunch?"

options.text: The student was asked by the teacher about bringing his lunch.
options.html: The student was asked by the teacher about bringing his lunch.

options.text: The teacher asked the student if he would be bringing his lunch.
options.html: The teacher asked the student if he would be bringing his lunch.

options.text: The teacher asked the student if he had brought his lunch.
options.html: The teacher asked the student if he had brought his lunch.

options.text: The teacher asked the student if he has brought his lunch.
options.html: The teacher asked the student if he has brought his lunch.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is The teacher asked the student if he had brought his lunch.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the question we have to change it into Indirect Speech. 
  • The process of transformation as follows: 
    • The given question is an example of an Interrogative sentence. 
    • 'Said to' will be changed into 'asked'. 
    • 'If' conjunction will be added to represent whether something is true or not
    • An interrogative statement is converted into an assertive statement. Thus, the helping verb will be placed after the subject.
    • 'You' will be changed into 'he'. (Second person->third person)
    • 'your' will be changed into 'his'.
    • 'Have' will be changed into 'had' (Present perfect tense->Past Perfect tense)
       

Therefore the correct answer is: The teacher asked the student if he had brought his lunch.
